input.content:
# Hypothesis

[T17-ROUND-1] Written by the first scheduled firing of the session schedule.
This file is the evidence that the second firing lands in the SAME workspace: it is
written once here, the session is then snapshotted and its container destroyed, and
the next firing has to restore the snapshot before it can read this line back.

[T17-MEMORY] Current state of the embedding hypothesis, written by a scheduled run of the long-lived session.

This body is deliberately much longer than five hundred bytes, because the point of writing it at all is to prove that the HTTP read route hands back the whole memory rather than the five-hundred-byte snippet the search route returns. A snippet is enough for a browser that is listing memories and about to link to one; it is not enough for an embedding application that wants to render the current state of a thing on its own page, which is the whole reason the by-name and current routes exist at all. So: the paragraph you are reading is padding with a purpose, and the assertion downstream is that every byte of it survives the round trip from the container, through the core MCP server, into Postgres and back out over HTTP to a caller holding nothing but a project API key. [T17-MEMORY-TAIL]
